blocks.text: Data is the foundation of data science: a collection of raw facts and values from which information is produced. It can be numbers, text, images, audio or video, and it is produced every day by many activities. Data must be understood before analysis, because different types need different handling; data must also be accurate and reliable, since poor data leads to wrong results.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Data quality strongly affects the final results; poor data can lead to incorrect conclusions.

blocks.caption: Two types of data
rows: A fixed, clear format of rows and columns
Easy to search and analyse directly
Hard to analyse directly; needs special tools

blocks.alt: Left panel, structured data: a small table with columns ID, Name and Age and rows 1 Basim 16, 2 Hina 17, 3 Ali 15; note: tables, spreadsheets, databases and mark sheets are easy to search and analyse. Right panel, unstructured data: simple icons for an email or text, an image, an audio wave and a video; note: needs special tools to analyse.
blocks.caption: Structured and unstructured data (original diagram after Fig 6.2).
blocks.long_description: Modern systems use both: a hospital keeps patient records in tables (structured) and X-ray images and doctors' notes (unstructured).

blocks.text: Data can be collected from many sources, such as surveys, interviews, forms and online platforms (blogs, social websites and others). Manual collection uses human effort; automatic collection uses machines and software, for example sensors. Data can be collected in real time or gathered over a period, depending on the purpose of the analysis. Good sources and accurate collection improve the quality of the analysis.

Data storage means saving data for future use in files, databases or the cloud; proper storage protects it from loss. Data management means organising and maintaining data so that it is easy to find and use. Security is an important part of management, and backup systems prevent data loss. Well-managed data is efficient and supports long-term use.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: Understanding the type of data properly is very important before analysing it.

blocks.prompt: Classify each as structured or unstructured: a class attendance register, a recorded lecture, a spreadsheet of fees, WhatsApp voice messages.
blocks.explanation: Structured: the attendance register and the fee spreadsheet (fixed rows and columns). Unstructured: the recorded lecture (video or audio) and the voice messages (audio).

items: Data: raw facts (numbers, text, images, audio, video); quality matters.
Structured: rows and columns; unstructured: no fixed format.
Collection: surveys, interviews, forms, online, sensors; storage: files, databases, cloud, with security and backup.
